title: Printing numbers without div
description:
Write a number printer that uses the magic-number division from this milestone instead of `div`, and check it against the routine you know.

```
0  7  42  1000  -250  9223372036854775807  -9223372036854775808
all 200 test values match print_int
```

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .bss
digits: resb    24

        section .text
_start:
        mov     rdi, 42
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline
        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: Work with the unsigned value of `-x` for negative numbers: for the most negative number, `neg` gives the same bits, which read as unsigned are the right magnitude (lesson 8.02).
Quotient and remainder both come from one multiply: `q = (x × magic) >> 67` and `r = x − q × 10`.
requirements: `print_signed(x)` converts to digits with multiply-by-magic division by 10, filling a buffer from the end, and writes it with one system call.
Handle 0, negative numbers and the most negative 64-bit number (which has no positive counterpart).
A test loop compares the output for many values with `print_int`'s (for example by building both into buffers).
stretch: Count the cycles for printing a million numbers with `rdtsc`, both ways.
